title: Timeboxed fallback orchestrator and regional holdoff (hotfix)
author: Marisol Vega
description:
Motivation: Over the last week we observed repeated SLO violations during regional failovers induced by an aggressive fast-reopen path in the fallback controller. Symptoms were rapid circuit flips, KV-cache drain collisions, and short-lived failovers that caused client retries and increased tail latency. This PR introduces a timeboxed fallback orchestrator that applies a short, configurable holdoff anchor when a region-level fallback is initiated. The goal is to reduce reopen flapping, give downstream systems (KV caches, routing tables) time to stabilize, and preserve the tenant SLOs while avoiding long hard-fail states.

What changed (high level):
- New orchestrator: src/runtime/fallback_orchestrator.go implements a timebox window (default 10s) during which reopen attempts are rate-limited and a soft circuit anchor is applied. The anchor prevents immediate reopen and coordinates with the SLO enforcer.
- Holdoff policy: pkg/slo/holdoff_policy.go introduces a small policy engine that selects a holdoff based on recent circuit history, tenant weight, and cross-region RTTs.
- KV cache drain sync: runtime/kv/drain_coordinator.go adds a two-phase drain handshake so we don't evict live KV entries during short failovers.
- Config toggle + feature-flag: config/defaults.yaml and infra/feature_flags/featureflags.go expose a canary flag (fallback_timebox_v2) so we can rollout per-region.
- Telemetry: observability/fallback_metrics.go emits new metrics (fallback_timebox_applied, fallback_anchor_duration_ms) and traces for the orchestrator's decision path.
- Tests: unit and integration tests + a small load canary harness under test/canary/fallback_timebox_test.go.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests added for policy branching; [x] Integration test for KV drain handshake; [x] Canary run in us-west-2 for 12 hours with synthetic spike; [x] Docs update in docs/ops/fallbacks.md; [x] Rollback plan documented.

Rollout and rollback: The rollout is behind an opt-in per-region flag. Default remains off. We performed a 12-hour canary in us-west-2 (see CI/canary logs) and then toggled additional regions sequentially with the console. Rollback is immediate: flip feature flag off and the orchestrator falls back to previous behavior; a short background reconciler drains anchors within 30s to avoid stale holds.

Backward compatibility & safety: No API changes. All behavior controlled by internal feature flags and a default conservative timebox. No tenant-visible config changes unless enterprise customers enable the flag.

Related linear/Jira: ENG-8743 tracks the broader SLO stabilization work; SUP-4421 was raised by on-call for a customer-facing incident.

Notes: This is marked as a hotfix because multiple incidents were traced to reopen flapping. The implementation prefers safety (slightly longer tail for some requests) to unstable reopen cycles that caused cascading retries.

review_comments: Alicia: Can we make the default window configurable via config and not a compile-time const? (resolved: made configurable in defaults.yaml)
Diego: The KV drain handshake looks racy when multiple regions trigger simultaneously — added a jitter and leader election attempt to the handshake (resolved)
Priya: Please add an integration test for tenant-weighted holdoff selection (added test and adjusted policy thresholds)
Marisol: Responded to Diego with a note about the leader-election fallback path and included instrumentation to detect failed handshakes for SRE visibility
ci_history: CI summary: initial CI run: build passed, unit tests passed, integration tests flaky (kv_drain_test timed out). Triggered a rerun after adding a 250ms jitter; subsequent CI: all checks passed. Canary: ran synthetic spike harness in us-west-2 for 12 hours; metrics validated.
release_notes: Hotfix: introduce timeboxed fallback orchestrator to reduce circuit reopen flapping during regional failovers. Default off behind feature flag. Improves SLO stability at the cost of a short holdoff during failovers. See docs/ops/fallbacks.md for runbook.
testing_performed: Unit tests for holdoff_policy and orchestrator logic. Integration test for KV drain coordinator handshake. Canary in us-west-2 for 12 hours with synthetic spike pattern (30s bursts every 2m). Load tests against canary nodes showed 18% reduction in reopen events and 9% improvement in 99th percentile latency during simulated failovers.
rollout_plan: Step 1: Enable fallback_timebox_v2 in a single small region (us-west-2) behind console flag and monitor for 12h. Step 2: Gradual expansion to other regions in 2x size increments with 6h monitoring windows. Step 3: If errors increase or KV drain handshake failures > 0.1% for 10m, roll back immediately (toggle off). All rollouts go through the infra feature-flag gate and change is reversible.
notes_for_support: If customers report longer request tails after enabling the flag, check: 1) fallback_timebox_applied metric; 2) fallback_anchor_duration_ms distribution; 3) kv_drain_handshake_failed counter. To rollback: flip feature flag to off via console or toggle API and restart reconciliation using admin endpoint /admin/fallback/reconcile. Attach logs: fallback_orch.trace and kv_drain.trace.
risk_assessment: medium - mitigations include feature flag gated rollout, conservative default timebox, and automated rollback thresholds. The orchestration logic is localized and does not modify public APIs.
notes: This PR was implemented as a hotfix after two related incidents; follow-up work will move holdoff decision thresholds into a telemetry-backed adaptive controller (tracked in ENG-8743).
